title: kernel-v1 audit-first LSM enforcement budget (v1)
description: Versioned source of truth for the numeric and policy constants that bound the audit-first BPF LSM deny engine (task 33: bpf/sensors/lsm.bpf.c). Every enforcement constant the bench harnesses and the kill-switch benchmark read is anchored here; any number not anchored here is a plan defect. The engine starts EVERY policy in audit-only mode (mode=0); a policy may only move to deny (mode=1) through the staged validated-map path (task 34), never inline. The kill-switch returns the policy map to deny-disabled within kill_switch_max_ms of the gRPC command reaching the agent; bench/kill-switch.sh measures the p99 over kill_switch_benchmark_pairs runs. The deny source recorded by the engine is OWN_LSM only when THIS BPF program returns an errno -- SELinux/AppArmor/another-BPF decisions are recorded as PRIOR_LSM and never relabeled OWN_LSM.

audit_first_default_mode.description: Mode every policy starts in. 0 = audit-only (the hook NEVER changes the syscall result; a matching selector emits an audit decision event with deny_source=none and returns 0). 1 = deny (a matching selector returns the policy errno and records an OWN_LSM_DENY event). The engine ships every policy at 0; only the staged validated-map path (task 34) may promote a policy to 1. This default is the audit-first invariant the bench harness asserts.

mode_audit.description: The mode value that means audit-only. Pinned to 0 so the C producer (lsm.bpf.c), the Rust agent mirror, and the bench harness agree on the encoding.

mode_deny.description: The mode value that means deny. Pinned to 1. A policy at mode=1 returns its deny_errno for an exact authoritative-selector match ONLY when the kill-switch is not engaged and no prior LSM has already decided (prior_ret == 0).

supported_hook_families.description: The LSM hook families the engine attaches and evaluates. file_open -> struct file path-prefix selector; bprm_check_security -> binary path selector (bprm->filename); socket_connect -> socket address selector (sockaddr). Any other hook family is unsupported and fails open (returns 0, no own-denial).

hook_family_file_open.description: Wire encoding of the file_open hook family in the LSM decision payload hook_family byte.

hook_family_bprm_check_security.description: Wire encoding of the bprm_check_security (binary exec) hook family in the LSM decision payload hook_family byte.

hook_family_socket_connect.description: Wire encoding of the socket_connect hook family in the LSM decision payload hook_family byte.

max_policy_entries.description: Number of slots in the lsm_policy BPF array map. The audit-first MVP keys one authoritative selector per hook family (slot 0 reserved/unused, slots 1..3 = file_open/bprm_check_security/socket_connect). The bounded single-lookup-per-family keeps the verifier path trivial; a future wave may widen to a multi-selector table via an ABI-compatible map bump.

selector_max_bytes.description: Maximum authoritative-selector size in bytes (KERNEL_V1_LSM_SELECTOR_MAX). A path prefix or sockaddr is bounded to this many bytes so an untrusted 4-KiB path argument cannot blow past the kernel-v1 payload budget. Selectors longer than this land in the truncation bucket and the policy is treated as no-match (fail-open).

lsm_payload_len.description: Fixed LSM decision payload size in bytes (KERNEL_V1_LSM_PAYLOAD_LEN). Every LSM decision record carries the union of fields at a uniform size so the consumer can dispatch on event_kind without first measuring the payload. Mirrors the file/network/dns fixed-payload precedent.

deny_errno_default.description: Default errno a deny-mode policy returns when it does not name an explicit errno. -13 = EACCES (permission denied). The engine returns the policy's configured deny_errno; this default is what the staged-map validator (task 34) fills in when a rule omits it. Always negative (an LSM deny is a negative errno).

kill_switch_max_ms.description: Maximum wall-clock milliseconds for the kill-switch to return the policy map to deny-disabled after the gRPC command reaches the agent. The kill-switch is a single lsm_kill_switch map slot; when deny_disabled=1 every deny-mode policy degrades to audit-only (returns 0) within this bound. bench/kill-switch.sh measures the p99 latency over kill_switch_benchmark_pairs runs and asserts p99 <= kill_switch_max_ms. This is the authoritative source the task acceptance criteria references as bench/schemas/enforcement.v1.json#kill_switch_max_ms.

kill_switch_benchmark_pairs.description: Number of engage/disengage benchmark pairs bench/kill-switch.sh runs to compute the p99 kill-switch latency. Each pair = one gRPC engage (deny_disabled=1) followed by one disengage (deny_disabled=0); the latency measured is engage-command-received -> map-reads-deny-disabled. Referenced as bench/schemas/enforcement.v1.json#kill_switch_benchmark_pairs.

fixture_min_precision_and_recall.description: Minimum precision and recall the enforcement decision logic must achieve on its declared synthetic fixture corpus (tests/fixtures/enforcement/). bench/enforcement-audit.sh reads this default; the value is NOT hardcoded in the harness. A fixture is a true positive when it expects an own-denial and the logic produces one; a true negative when it expects no own-denial (audit/allow/preserve/fail-open) and the logic produces none.
